newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil publishes approval of coffee harvest funds.
newsitem.headline: Brazil publishes approval of coffee harvest funds.

text.p: Brazil's government gazette Tuesday published the authorization of a 250 million reais (US$234 million) credit line for this year's coffee harvest.
The financing, to come from the Funcafe coffee fund, was approved "ad referendum" by the country's National Monetary Council and will start to be released this month.

For those areas with normal crop development, 60 percent of credit will be made available in May and the remainder in June. Farmers in other regions where the coffee trees mature later can apply for the bulk of financing in June.
Repayment will be at Brazil's long-term interest rate (TJLP) plus three percent.
Brazil's new coffee council, the CDPC, approved the funds at a meeting earlier this month which looked at the future of the coffee sector and producer debt.

Following the authorisation of the harvest funds, council members over the coming months are to examine proposals for further credit lines for stock financing and preparing for next year's crop. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
